common_name: Bush Delicata Squash (Compact Vine Delicata for Small Beds)

planting.note: Sow after all danger of frost has passed and soil has warmed; Bush Delicata forms a compact, short-vined plant that fits raised beds and small gardens where a standard sprawling delicata vine would take up far too much room.

directions: Sow seed an inch deep in warm, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, spacing plants 2 to 3 feet apart since the compact bush habit needs far less room than a standard vining delicata. Bush Delicata produces the same sweet, creamy, striped-skinned fruit prized in classic delicata squash, but on a tidy, short-vined plant that stays contained rather than rambling 6 to 10 feet like the traditional vining type, making it a good fit for raised beds, small gardens, or anywhere space is at a premium. Provide steady, even moisture through flowering and fruit set, and mulch around the base to conserve water and suppress weeds. Harvest once the rind hardens and the cream-and-green stripes deepen in color, then cure fruits in a warm, dry spot for a week or two before storing to concentrate their sweetness and extend keeping quality.
